newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein higher after pact.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein higher after pact.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were higher in late trading on Thursday after traders struck a deal to raise offer prices, traders said.

They said olein was quoted at 1,485-90 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, up from last done 1,460-65 rupiah. Crude palm oil was heard done at 1,303 rupiah/kg in the North Sumatran city of Medan, matching Wednesday's tender price. It was previously done at 1,270.

Traders and refiners agreed at an informal meeting on Wednesday night in Jakarta to raise the offer price of palm olein to 1,500 rupiah from this morning due to the relatively high price of crude palm oil.
"But not everyone was keeping to the understanding reached last night," one trader said. "There was selling at 1,485 rupiah and 1,490 rupiah. I guess it's up to individual companies."
Traders said the consensus was reached because there was no margin in processing crude palm oil for the local market due to the relatively low olein price.
"With crude palm oil at around 1,300 rupiah, olein must be sold at 1,480 rupiah the least for refiners to make a margin," one trader said.
"But when I was offering olein at 1,500 rupiah, there were no takers," he said.
Traders also said the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on the market.
"He has been ill for a long time, and his death was not totally unexpected," one trader said.
Traders also said China buys most of its crude palm oil products from neighbouring Malaysia.
